name: Civil Service core vocabulary
description: The 100 terms a civil servant needs to know, from the first day as an Administrative Officer to the Senior Civil Service.

groups.grade: Civil Service grade or career term

cards.subject: civil servant
says: is a permanent official who helps the government of the day develop and deliver its policies
stays in post when the government changes
cards.use: talk about the permanent staff who serve every government
not: is an elected politician who is chosen by voters

cards.subject: minister
says: is an elected politician, or a peer, appointed to lead work in a department
is accountable to Parliament for the policy of that department
cards.use: need to know who takes the political decisions in a department
not: is a permanent official who stays when the government changes

cards.subject: Secretary of State
says: is the minister who heads a government department
sits at the top of a department's ministerial team
cards.use: need to name the most senior minister in a department
not: is the most senior permanent official in a department

cards.subject: Permanent Secretary
says: is the most senior civil servant in a department
gives the Secretary of State impartial advice and leads the department's staff
cards.use: need to name the most senior official who leads the department's civil servants
not: is elected to Parliament by voters

cards.subject: department
says: is a government organisation led by a Secretary of State
develops and delivers policy in a particular area such as health or transport
cards.use: talk about an organisation like the Home Office or the Treasury
not: is a committee of MPs that scrutinises the government

cards.subject: Cabinet Office
says: supports the Prime Minister and the Cabinet
helps the government's departments work together
cards.use: need the central department that supports the Prime Minister and coordinates government
not: sets the limits on public spending

cards.subject: HM Treasury
says: is the government department responsible for public spending and economic policy
agrees the spending limits that other departments must work within
cards.use: need to know who controls public spending across government
not: supports the Cabinet and coordinates the work of departments

cards.subject: Civil Service Code
says: sets out the four values of integrity, honesty, objectivity and impartiality
describes the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants
cards.use: need to know the values civil servants must follow
not: is a code that sets the pay bands for each grade

cards.subject: impartiality
says: means acting solely on the merits of the case
means serving governments of different political parties equally well
cards.use: are asked to serve a new government that you did not vote for
not: means supporting the governing party in public

cards.subject: special adviser
says: is a temporary political appointee who advises a minister
leaves when their minister leaves, and is not bound by the duty of impartiality
cards.use: need to name the political adviser who works for a minister rather than the department
not: is a permanent official who must stay impartial

cards.subject: Administrative Officer
says: is an entry grade for routine administrative work
works from guidance and procedures under regular supervision
cards.use: start in a role handling enquiries or cases by following guidance
not: leads a policy area and manages managers

cards.subject: Executive Officer
says: runs a caseload or a small area of work with some independence
may supervise a few colleagues
cards.use: run a caseload with some independence
not: is a senior leadership grade that sits above Grade 6

cards.subject: Higher Executive Officer
says: is typically the first grade that formally manages a team or leads a specialist area
contributes to plans and advice
cards.use: manage a team or lead a specialist area for the first time
not: works only from guidance and is never responsible for others

cards.subject: Senior Executive Officer
says: leads a larger team or a significant piece of work
advises more senior colleagues
cards.use: lead a bigger team or a significant piece of work that is below Grade 7 level
not: is the first grade at which anyone is asked to supervise others

cards.subject: Grade 7
says: leads a policy, delivery or operational area
manages managers and prepares advice for senior leaders
cards.use: manage managers and prepare advice for senior leaders
not: is an entry grade that works from guidance

cards.subject: Grade 6
says: leads a large area of work and its senior managers
advises directors and ministers' offices
cards.use: lead a large area and advise directors
not: is the grade just above the Administrative Officer grade

cards.subject: Senior Civil Service
says: is the senior leadership group of Deputy Directors and above
is set apart from the grades below it with its own pay and recruitment arrangements
cards.use: talk about leaders at Deputy Director level and above
not: is the group of entry-level grades below Executive Officer

cards.subject: Fast Stream
says: is an accelerated development programme for graduates
moves people through different postings to build leadership skills quickly
cards.use: want a graduate scheme that moves people between postings to build leadership skills fast
not: is a type of urgent security check

cards.subject: Success Profiles
says: is the framework used to assess candidates for civil service jobs
combines behaviours, strengths, ability, experience and technical skills
cards.use: are preparing for a civil service application and need the assessment framework
not: is a list of the pay points for each grade

cards.subject: Civil Service Commission
says: regulates recruitment so that it follows fair and open competition on merit
hears complaints that the Civil Service Code has been breached
cards.use: need to know who protects merit-based recruitment and the Civil Service Code
not: decides government policy for the Civil Service

cards.subject: submission
says: is written advice that asks a minister to make a decision or give agreement
sets out the issue, the options and a recommendation
cards.use: need a minister to make a decision
not: is an answer given to a question from an MP

cards.subject: private office
says: is the team that supports a minister's day-to-day work
manages the flow of papers and advice between the minister and the department
cards.use: need to send something urgently to a minister
not: is the team that reports to Parliament on spending

cards.subject: private secretary
says: manages a minister's diary and the flow of papers and advice to them
works as a link between the minister and the department
cards.use: need to talk to the person who handles a minister's diary and papers
not: is a politician who is employed by the governing party

cards.subject: ministerial correspondence
says: is the letters and emails sent to a minister by MPs and the public
is drafted by officials for the minister to sign or approve
cards.use: need to prepare a reply for a minister to send to a member of the public
not: is advice that asks the minister for a decision

cards.subject: line to take
says: is an agreed answer to a likely question
keeps everyone who speaks for the department saying the same thing
cards.use: need agreed answers ready before a media interview
not: is a rule about who can be a candidate in an election

cards.subject: ministerial briefing
says: gives a minister the facts and background they need before a meeting or event
is prepared by officials in a short, clear format
cards.use: need to prepare a minister to speak at an event
not: asks the minister to choose between options

cards.subject: red box
says: is the box of papers that a minister takes away to work through outside the office
contains submissions and other items needing their attention
cards.use: hear that a minister has papers to read overnight
not: is a secure room where Cabinet meets

cards.subject: Parliamentary question
says: is a question put by a member of Parliament to a minister
needs a reply drafted by officials and agreed by the minister
cards.use: are asked to draft an answer to a question from an MP
not: is a vote taken in the House of Commons

cards.subject: pre-election period
says: is the time before an election when departments avoid new major policy announcements
is often called purdah
cards.use: see an election called while a department plans a big new policy announcement
not: is the period after an election when ministers are chosen

cards.subject: ministerial direction
says: is a written instruction from a minister that an accounting officer asked for before going ahead
is copied to the Comptroller and Auditor General
cards.use: object that a minister's spending plan fails a spending test but the minister insists
not: is a speech made by a minister in the House of Commons

cards.subject: House of Commons
says: is the elected chamber of Parliament
is where MPs sit
cards.use: need to name the chamber that MPs belong to
not: is the chamber of appointed members and hereditary peers

cards.subject: House of Lords
says: is the chamber of Parliament made up of appointed and some hereditary members
revises bills sent from the Commons
cards.use: need to name the chamber that revises legislation but is not elected
not: is the chamber that MPs are elected to

cards.subject: bill
says: is a proposed law that is going through Parliament
can be amended as it passes between the two Houses
cards.use: talk about a draft law that has not yet been passed
not: is a law that has already come into force

cards.subject: Act of Parliament
says: is a law that has passed through Parliament and received Royal Assent
can give ministers powers to make detailed rules
cards.use: need to name a law that Parliament has passed
not: is a proposed law still being debated

cards.subject: Royal Assent
says: is the monarch's formal agreement that turns a bill into an Act
comes after both Houses have agreed the bill
cards.use: want to know the final step that turns a bill into law
not: is the vote in the Commons that gives a bill its first reading

cards.subject: statutory instrument
says: is a form of secondary legislation made under powers given by an Act
sets out detailed rules without a new Act having to be passed
cards.use: need to set detailed rules using powers an Act has already given
not: is a bill that has been through all stages in the Lords

cards.subject: Hansard
says: is the official report of what is said in Parliament
records debates in both Houses
cards.use: need to find exactly what a minister said in the Commons
not: is a guide to what a department must do to meet its targets

cards.subject: select committee
says: is a group of MPs or peers that examines a department's work
can call ministers and officials to give evidence
cards.use: are asked to give evidence to a group of MPs about your department
not: is a team of officials that supports a minister

cards.subject: Public Accounts Committee
says: is a committee of MPs that examines whether public spending gave value for money
is supported by the National Audit Office
cards.use: need to name the committee that scrutinises the value for money of public spending
not: is a committee that decides how much each department receives

cards.subject: State Opening of Parliament
says: marks the start of a new session of Parliament
includes the monarch's speech setting out the government's plans for new laws
cards.use: want to know when the government announces its legislative plans for the year
not: is the final day on which a bill can be amended

cards.subject: policy
says: is a course of action that a government chooses to follow
is decided by ministers on advice from officials
cards.use: talk about a government's chosen approach to an issue
not: is a law that has been passed by Parliament

cards.subject: policy cycle
says: describes the stages from spotting a problem to evaluating a policy
runs from rationale and objectives through appraisal, implementation and evaluation
cards.use: need to describe the stages policy goes through
not: is the set of dates on which Parliament sits

cards.subject: green paper
says: is a consultation document that sets out proposals not yet decided
invites views before the government settles on its policy
cards.use: want views on ideas that the government has not yet decided on
not: sets out firm proposals that are about to become law

cards.subject: white paper
says: sets out the government's firm proposals for future policy
often comes before a bill is introduced
cards.use: need to publish firm proposals before introducing a bill
not: is an early document that only asks for views on ideas

cards.subject: public consultation
says: asks the public, experts and organisations for their views on a proposal
has to be fair and carried out at a formative stage
cards.use: need to hear from people affected before a decision
not: is a vote that decides a policy

cards.subject: impact assessment
says: assesses the costs, benefits and risks of a proposed policy or regulation
helps decision-makers compare options
cards.use: need to show what a new regulation will cost and who it will affect
not: checks whether a past policy worked

cards.subject: options appraisal
says: compares the possible ways of meeting an objective
weighs costs, benefits and risks of each option
cards.use: need to compare several ways of meeting an objective before recommending one
not: decides which minister will announce the policy

cards.subject: stakeholder
says: is a person or group affected by a decision or able to influence it
may include the public, businesses, charities and other departments
cards.use: need to identify who will be affected by or can influence a decision
not: is a person who owns shares in a company

cards.subject: pilot
says: tests a policy or service on a small scale before it is rolled out widely
lets a team learn what works before spending more
cards.use: want to test an idea with a small group before a national launch
not: is the final report on whether a policy succeeded

cards.subject: evaluation
says: judges after the event whether a policy worked and why
feeds lessons back into future policy
cards.use: need to find out whether a policy delivered what was intended
not: is the first stage in which ministers decide to act

cards.subject: Spending Review
says: sets departments' budgets over several years
is led by HM Treasury
cards.use: need to know how much a department will have for the next few years
not: is the audit of last year's accounts

cards.subject: Supply Estimate
says: is a request to Parliament for the money and authority a department needs
is voted on by MPs before the department can spend it
cards.use: need Parliament to authorise a department's spending for the year
not: is a published report on past spending

cards.subject: Managing Public Money
says: is HM Treasury's guidance on handling public funds properly
sets out the standards for regularity, propriety, value for money and feasibility
cards.use: need guidance on how to handle public money correctly
not: is a guide to how decisions are appraised using the five cases

cards.subject: Green Book
says: is HM Treasury's guidance on appraising and evaluating policies, programmes and projects
underpins the way business cases are prepared
cards.use: need the guidance that explains how to appraise a proposal before spending public money
not: is the guidance on how to keep accounts

cards.subject: accounting officer
says: is personally accountable to Parliament for how their organisation uses public money
is normally the Permanent Secretary in a department
cards.use: need to know who answers to Parliament for how the department spends its money
not: is the person who prepares the annual accounts

cards.subject: value for money
says: means the best balance of cost, quality and outcomes
is not the same as choosing the cheapest option
cards.use: want the best overall result for the money spent
not: means always choosing the cheapest option

cards.subject: regularity
says: means spending complies with the legislation and authority that governs it
is one of the tests applied to a proposal by an accounting officer
cards.use: need to confirm that spending is lawful and approved
not: means spending is delivered at the lowest possible price

cards.subject: propriety
says: means spending meets Parliament's standards of conduct, fairness and honesty
is a test that goes beyond whether the spending is merely legal
cards.use: worry that spending is legal but would not meet Parliament's standards of conduct
not: means spending is approved by a majority vote

cards.subject: Five Case Model
says: structures a business case in strategic, economic, commercial, financial and management cases
is used to show a proposal is worth funding
cards.use: need a structure for a business case
not: is the five stages a bill goes through in Parliament

cards.subject: National Audit Office
says: is an independent body that audits government spending for Parliament
reports on whether departments have achieved value for money
cards.use: need the independent auditor of government spending
not: is a department that sets the spending budgets

cards.subject: Freedom of Information request
says: asks a public authority for recorded information that it holds
normally has to be answered within 20 working days
cards.use: receive a request from a member of the public for information the department holds
not: asks to see the personal data held about the person who asked

cards.subject: subject access request
says: asks an organisation for a copy of the personal data it holds about the requester
normally has to be answered within one month
cards.use: get a request from someone to see the personal data held about them
not: asks for general information that the department holds

cards.subject: judicial review
says: is a court process that tests whether a public body's decision was lawful
looks at the way a decision was made rather than whether the policy is wise
cards.use: hear a charity claim that a department made a decision unlawfully
not: is a review of a department's accounts by the audit office

cards.subject: public sector equality duty
says: requires public bodies to have due regard to equality when they make decisions
comes from the Equality Act
cards.use: need to consider the effect of a decision on people with protected characteristics
not: is the duty to publish accounts

cards.subject: statutory duty
says: is something a public body must do because a law requires it
can be enforced through the courts if it is ignored
cards.use: find that a law says the department must do something
not: is a power that a body may choose to use or ignore

cards.subject: Seven Principles of Public Life
says: sets out seven standards for people in public life
includes selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability, openness, honesty and leadership
cards.use: need the seven standards often known as the Nolan principles
not: sets out the four values of the Civil Service Code

cards.subject: whistleblowing
says: is reporting suspected wrongdoing inside an organisation
is supported by routes such as a line manager or a nominated officer
cards.use: suspect that a colleague is committing fraud
not: is making a complaint about the service you received

cards.subject: conflict of interest
says: arises when a personal interest could affect, or look like it affects, official judgement
needs to be declared and managed
cards.use: find that your relative works for a bidder on a contract you are judging
not: is a legal claim brought against the department

cards.subject: Ombudsman
says: investigates complaints that poor service or mistakes by a public body caused injustice
is independent of the body being complained about
cards.use: see a citizen use up a department's complaints process and still feel wronged
not: decides whether a decision was lawful and can quash it

cards.subject: legal professional privilege
says: protects confidential communications between a lawyer and their client
normally means legal advice need not be disclosed
cards.use: are asked to release legal advice that the department received
not: allows lawyers to keep documents from ministers

cards.subject: Service Standard
says: is a set of points that government digital services are expected to meet
is assessed at points such as the end of alpha and beta
cards.use: need to know what a government digital service is expected to meet
not: is a list of the grades of civil servants

cards.subject: user need
says: is what a person needs to do, described from their point of view
comes before decisions about the solution
cards.use: need to understand what people actually need before choosing a solution
not: is a technical requirement written by the supplier

cards.subject: discovery
says: is the phase in which a team learns about users and the problem
happens before any decision to build
cards.use: need to understand the problem and users before deciding what to build
not: is the phase in which a working service is tested with real users

cards.subject: alpha
says: is the phase where a team builds prototypes and tests possible solutions
comes after discovery
cards.use: need to test several prototype solutions
not: is the phase in which a team learns about users before choosing a solution

cards.subject: beta
says: is the phase where a team builds a working service and tests it with limited real users
comes before the service goes live
cards.use: need to run a working service with a limited group of real users
not: is the phase where a team tests early prototypes with a small group

cards.subject: agile
says: delivers work in short cycles with regular feedback
adjusts the plan as the team learns
cards.use: want to deliver work in small steps and adapt as you learn
not: fixes the whole plan and scope at the start and leaves them unchanged

cards.subject: GOV.UK
says: is the single website for government services and information
replaced many separate departmental websites
cards.use: need to find government services in one place
not: is the website of Parliament

cards.subject: senior responsible owner
says: is the person accountable for the delivery of a project and its benefits
is named at the start of a major project
cards.use: need to know who is accountable for a major project's success
not: is the lead for day-to-day tasks within a work package

cards.subject: Gateway review
says: is an independent assurance review of a project at a key point
helps senior leaders judge whether a project is likely to succeed
cards.use: need an independent view on whether a project is on track
not: is a security check on people working on a project

cards.subject: benefits realisation
says: is making sure the expected benefits of a project actually happen
continues after delivery is finished
cards.use: find that a project was delivered on time but nobody is tracking the expected savings
not: is the process of choosing a supplier

cards.subject: OFFICIAL
says: is the classification for most routine public-sector business
is the lowest of the three government security classifications
cards.use: handle ordinary day-to-day government information
not: is reserved for information that could seriously threaten national security

cards.subject: OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE
says: is a handling caveat added to OFFICIAL information that needs extra care
is used for things like sensitive personal data
cards.use: share a spreadsheet that contains sensitive personal data
not: is a classification above SECRET

cards.subject: SECRET
says: is for very sensitive information where compromise would seriously harm national security or serious crime investigations
needs stronger protection than OFFICIAL
cards.use: handle very sensitive material that needs strong protection
not: covers most routine business and can be shared widely

cards.subject: need to know
says: means only people who need information for their job should be given it
applies even when a person holds the right clearance
cards.use: are asked by a cleared colleague to see papers that they have no role in
not: means everyone with clearance can see everything at the same level

cards.subject: Baseline Personnel Security Standard
says: is the set of baseline checks on identity, right to work, employment history and unspent convictions
is a minimum pre-employment check
cards.use: need the minimum checks that every new starter has to pass
not: is the highest level of vetting available

cards.subject: Security Check
says: is a level of vetting for people who need long-term access to SECRET material
goes further than the baseline standard
cards.use: need to be cleared for regular access to SECRET information
not: is the lowest level of pre-employment checking

cards.subject: Developed Vetting
says: is the highest level of personnel vetting
includes detailed checks and interviews
cards.use: need to be cleared for the most sensitive work
not: is the minimum check carried out for every new starter

cards.subject: Official Secrets Act
says: is a law that makes unauthorised disclosure of certain official information a criminal offence
applies to civil servants and others who hold official information
cards.use: need to remember the law that criminalises unauthorised disclosure of some official information
not: is the law that gives the public a right to request information

cards.subject: information asset owner
says: is a senior person responsible for a set of information and how it is used and protected
reports risks to the senior information risk owner
cards.use: need to name the person responsible for a set of data and how it is protected
not: is the person who writes the department's website content

cards.subject: National Archives
says: is the official archive for the UK government
keeps selected public records for permanent preservation
cards.use: need to know where selected public records are kept permanently
not: is the committee that scrutinises records

cards.subject: Deputy Director
says: leads a group of teams in a department
is typically the first grade in the Senior Civil Service
cards.use: need to name the first Senior Civil Service grade
not: is the most senior civil servant in a department

cards.subject: Director General
says: leads a group of directorates in a department
reports to the Permanent Secretary
cards.use: need to name the senior leader in charge of a large part of the department
not: is the head of the whole Civil Service

cards.subject: Cabinet Secretary
says: is the Prime Minister's principal civil service adviser
supports the Cabinet and its committees
cards.use: need to name the senior official who supports the Cabinet
not: is a minister who sits in the Cabinet

cards.subject: machinery of government change
says: moves functions or responsibilities between departments
can create a new department or merge departments
cards.use: find that a function moves from one department to another
not: is a change to the way that Parliament votes

cards.subject: departmental board
says: brings together ministers, senior officials and non-executives to oversee a department
advises on strategy, performance and risk
cards.use: need the forum that oversees a department's strategy and performance
not: is a committee of MPs that scrutinises a department

cards.subject: non-executive board member
says: is an external expert who challenges and advises a department's board
is not a full-time member of the department's staff
cards.use: need an outside voice to challenge a department's strategy
not: is a minister who sits on the board

cards.subject: arm's length body
says: is a public body that works at a distance from ministers
covers both executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies
cards.use: need an umbrella term for public bodies that sit apart from the department
not: is a team inside a minister's private office

cards.subject: executive agency
says: is part of a department but has its own chief executive
delivers a specific service and works under a framework document
cards.use: need to name a part of a department that delivers a service with its own chief executive
not: is a public body that is not part of any department

cards.subject: non-departmental public body
says: carries out a government function at arm's length from ministers
is not itself a government department or part of one
cards.use: need to name a public body that is separate from departments
not: is a part of a department with its own chief executive

cards.subject: government function
says: is a cross-government network that sets standards for a profession such as finance or digital
is led by a senior official who looks after that profession
cards.use: need to know who sets standards for a profession across all departments
not: is a department that delivers services to the public

qa.q: Who decides government policy?
qa.why: Ministers decide policy; civil servants advise and carry it out.

qa.q: What are the four values in the Civil Service Code?
qa.why: These four values are set out in the Civil Service Code.

qa.q: A new government is elected. What happens to civil servants?
qa.right: They continue to serve the new government impartially
wrong: They serve only the party they voted for
They wait for the Civil Service Commission to approve the new ministers
qa.why: Civil servants serve the government of the day, whichever party it is.

qa.q: What do baseline personnel security checks normally cover?
qa.right: Identity, right to work, employment history and unspent criminal convictions
qa.why: The baseline standard checks identity, right to work, history and unspent convictions.

qa.q: A member of the public asks a department for recorded information it holds. Which law gives them that right?
qa.why: The Freedom of Information Act gives a right to request recorded information.

qa.q: Which classification covers most routine public-sector business?
qa.why: OFFICIAL covers ordinary day-to-day government information.

qa.q: What is a submission?
qa.right: Written advice that asks a minister to make a decision
wrong: A formal complaint about a minister
An answer to a question from an MP
A statement of a department's costs
qa.why: A submission sets out the issue and options and asks for a decision.

qa.q: An MP asks a minister a written question about a department's work. What is this?
qa.why: A Parliamentary question needs an answer from the minister.

qa.q: Which document consults on proposals that the government has not yet decided?
qa.why: A green paper invites views on options; a white paper sets out firm proposals.

qa.q: Which publication sets out the government's firm proposals before a bill is introduced?
qa.why: A white paper contains firm proposals.

qa.q: Where would you find the official record of what a minister said in the House of Commons?
qa.why: Hansard is the official report of debates in Parliament.

qa.q: What does 'value for money' mean?
qa.right: The best balance of cost and quality in achieving the intended outcome
wrong: Choosing the highest quality whatever it costs
Spending the whole budget before the year ends
qa.why: Value for money is not the same as lowest cost.

qa.q: What does a stakeholder mean in policy work?
qa.right: A person or group that is affected by or can influence a decision
wrong: A person who owns shares in a company
A minister who has been appointed to a department
A lawyer who advises on the policy
qa.why: Stakeholders include anyone affected by or able to influence the decision.

qa.q: Which person is appointed by a minister, leaves when the minister leaves and is not bound by impartiality?
qa.why: Special advisers are temporary political appointees.

qa.q: You are asked to prepare advice on a policy you personally disagree with. What should a civil servant do?
qa.right: Give honest, evidence-based advice and then help to implement the decision taken
wrong: Soften the evidence so the minister will drop it
qa.why: Civil servants give impartial advice and carry out the decisions of ministers.

qa.q: Which phase of a digital service is for learning about users and the problem before deciding what to build?
qa.why: Discovery comes before alpha and beta.

qa.q: Which phase builds a working service and tests it with limited real users?
qa.why: Beta is a working service used by limited real users.

qa.q: Before finalising a policy, a department asks the public and experts for their views. What is this?
qa.why: A public consultation gathers views from those affected.

qa.q: Who is accountable to Parliament for the policy of a department?
qa.why: Ministers are accountable to Parliament for policy.

qa.q: You suspect a colleague is falsifying expense claims. What should you do?
qa.right: Report it through your line manager or the department's route for raising concerns
wrong: Confront them in front of the team
Say nothing in case you are wrong
qa.why: The Civil Service Code supports raising concerns through proper routes.

qa.q: You are on a panel choosing a supplier and the bidder employs your sister. What do you do?
qa.right: Declare it to your manager and step back from the decision
wrong: Say nothing as you are impartial
qa.why: A conflict of interest must be declared and managed.

qa.q: A person asks a department for a copy of all the personal data it holds about them. What is this?
qa.why: A subject access request is a request for your own personal data.

qa.q: A colleague with the right clearance asks to see a SECRET paper out of curiosity. What should you do?
qa.right: Refuse, because access also depends on need to know
wrong: Share it, as they have clearance
Show it only if they promise to keep it quiet
Send it to them by email
qa.why: Clearance is not enough on its own; the person must also need to know.

qa.q: A spreadsheet of staff medical details is to be shared inside the department. How should it be marked?
qa.why: Sensitive personal data needs the OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE caveat.

qa.q: A body delivers a service, has its own chief executive and is part of a department. What type of body is it?
qa.why: Executive agencies are part of a department with their own chief executive.

qa.q: Who is accountable for the delivery of a major project and its benefits?
qa.why: The SRO is the accountable individual.

qa.q: Which guidance explains how to appraise and evaluate proposals before public money is spent?
qa.why: The Green Book is the Treasury's guidance on appraisal and evaluation.

qa.q: What does regularity mean for public spending?
qa.right: The spending complies with the law and the authority that governs it
wrong: The spending is as cheap as possible
The spending has been approved by a public vote
qa.why: Regularity is about legal authority and compliance.

qa.q: Which structure organises a business case into strategic, economic, commercial, financial and management cases?
qa.why: The Five Case Model is the standard business case structure.

qa.q: Which Treasury-led process sets departments' budgets over several years?
qa.why: A Spending Review sets multi-year departmental budgets.

qa.q: An accounting officer thinks a minister's spending plan fails the propriety test but the minister insists. What can they ask for?
wrong: A ruling from a select committee
qa.why: The accounting officer can ask for a written direction before going ahead.

qa.q: A general election has been called and a department wants to announce a major new policy. What should it do?
qa.right: Avoid announcing it during the pre-election period unless it cannot wait
wrong: Announce it immediately to help the governing party
qa.why: Departments avoid new major announcements before an election.

qa.q: A project finishes on time and on budget but nobody is checking whether the savings have happened. What is missing?
qa.why: Benefits realisation tracks whether the expected benefits happen.

qa.q: A charity says a department made a decision unlawfully. Which court process could test this?
qa.why: A judicial review tests the lawfulness of decisions.

qa.q: A citizen has used up a department's complaints process and still feels wronged. Who may investigate next?
qa.right: The Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman, usually through an MP
qa.why: The Ombudsman investigates unresolved complaints of maladministration.

qa.q: A team assesses the effect of a new rule on groups who share protected characteristics before introducing it. Which duty are they meeting?
qa.why: The duty requires due regard to equality when making decisions.

qa.q: A Grade 7 finds that a project's benefits will not be delivered as planned. What should they do?
qa.right: Escalate to the senior responsible owner with evidence and options
wrong: Hide it until the next review
Wait for the National Audit Office to find it
qa.why: Problems should be escalated early with options.

qa.q: A function moves from one department to another after a reorganisation. What is this?
qa.why: Machinery of government changes move functions between departments.

qa.q: Which committee examines whether public spending gave value for money, supported by the National Audit Office?
qa.why: The PAC scrutinises value for money and is supported by the NAO.

qa.q: A minister uses powers given by an Act to set detailed rules without a new Act. What is the instrument?
qa.why: Statutory instruments are secondary legislation made under an Act's powers.

qa.q: A department makes a decision. Which of these can a judicial review examine?
qa.right: Whether the decision was lawful, rational and procedurally fair
wrong: Whether the court prefers a different policy
Whether the minister's party supports it
qa.why: A judicial review looks at how a decision was made, not whether it is wise.

qa.q: An independent body audits department accounts and reports on value for money to Parliament. What is it?
qa.why: The NAO audits spending for Parliament.

qa.q: A select committee asks a senior official to give evidence about a department's performance. What is this?
qa.right: Part of Parliament's scrutiny of the department
wrong: A judicial review of the department
qa.why: Select committees scrutinise departments and can call officials.

qa.q: A senior official is asked to release legal advice the department received. What protects it?
qa.why: Legal advice is normally protected by privilege.

qa.q: Which forum brings ministers, senior officials and non-executives together to oversee a department's strategy, performance and risk?
qa.why: The departmental board oversees strategy, performance and risk.

qa.q: Who is the Prime Minister's principal civil service adviser and supports the Cabinet and its committees?
wrong: The Governor of the Bank of England
qa.why: The Cabinet Secretary supports the Cabinet and advises the Prime Minister.

qa.q: A department wants an independent view on whether a major project is likely to succeed. What should it commission?
qa.why: A Gateway review is an independent assurance of a project.

qa.q: Spending is within the law but would breach Parliament's standards of fairness and honesty. Which test would it fail?
qa.why: Propriety concerns the standards of conduct that Parliament expects.

qa.q: Who sets standards for a profession such as finance or digital across every department?
qa.why: Government functions set cross-government standards for professions.

qa.q: Who is responsible for a set of information and how it is used and protected, reporting risks to the senior information risk owner?
qa.why: Information asset owners are responsible for a defined set of information.

termBank.name: Civil Service core
termBank.description: What a civil servant needs to know, from the first day to the Senior Civil Service.
